categories.name: Study Apps
categories.description: Apps for drilling code words, Q codes, and call signs.
categories.descriptionLong: Use these apps to practice the NATO alphabet and radio phrases away from a desk. Look for downloads that work offline and decks you can add your own words to.

subcategories.name: Flashcard Apps
subcategories.description: Spaced repetition decks for code words and phrases.
subcategories.descriptionLong: Flashcard apps show a prompt and ask for the answer, then schedule another review based on how you did. They suit letter to code word pairs, Q codes, and short radio phrases.

subcategories.name: Reference Apps
subcategories.description: Quick lookup of code words and abbreviations.
subcategories.descriptionLong: Use these references to check a code word, a Morse assignment, or the meaning of a procedural abbreviation during practice.

subcategories.name: All-in-One Practice
subcategories.description: Apps that mix drills, guides, and progress tracking.
subcategories.descriptionLong: These resources combine reading material with drills, so you can look up a rule and then practice it in the same place.

subcategories.name: Typing Tools
subcategories.description: Practice entering call signs and typed responses.
subcategories.descriptionLong: Typing drills help when you need to record a call sign or answer a written exercise. Use them alongside spoken practice.

categories.name: Websites
categories.description: Reference and course sites for radio phraseology.
categories.descriptionLong: These sites cover the alphabet, procedural words, and the rules behind voice communication. Most are free to read and work in any browser.

subcategories.name: Guided Courses
subcategories.description: Structured material for step by step study.
subcategories.descriptionLong: Start here if you want an ordered path through licensing, phraseology, or code practice.

subcategories.name: Reference Sites
subcategories.description: Articles and tables to check facts quickly.
subcategories.descriptionLong: Bookmark these pages for code word lists, abbreviation tables, and explanations of standard procedure.

subcategories.name: Practice Sites
subcategories.description: Places to ask questions and test what you know.
subcategories.descriptionLong: Use forums, card sets, and lookup tools to check your recall and get answers from other operators.

categories.name: Books & Manuals
categories.description: Handbooks, manuals, and long form guides for radio work.
categories.descriptionLong: Printed manuals and official handbooks give you material that is easy to mark up and revisit. Many publishers also sell digital editions.

subcategories.name: Introductory Books
subcategories.description: First books for new operators and pilots.
subcategories.descriptionLong: These titles introduce licensing, basic equipment, and the first radio calls without assuming prior experience.

subcategories.name: Intermediate Guides
subcategories.description: Books for learners with the basics covered.
subcategories.descriptionLong: These guides go deeper into procedures, reading comprehension, and the wording of standard calls.

subcategories.name: Advanced Guides
subcategories.description: Material for detailed technical study.
subcategories.descriptionLong: Use these references when you want to understand the rules and technical background behind radio practice.

subcategories.name: Specialist Books
subcategories.description: Books focused on one part of radio work.
subcategories.descriptionLong: Pick a single subject, such as Morse code, distress procedures, or call signs, and study it in detail.

categories.name: Video Channels
categories.description: Video lessons and demonstrations about radio communication.
categories.descriptionLong: Video makes it easier to hear pronunciation and timing. The channels and search pages below collect lessons on the alphabet, Morse code, and phraseology.

subcategories.name: Lessons & Explanations
subcategories.description: Channels and playlists that teach step by step.
subcategories.descriptionLong: Watch a short lesson, then repeat the words or phrases out loud before moving on.

subcategories.name: Context & History
subcategories.description: Background on how radio communication is used.
subcategories.descriptionLong: These videos show the settings where the alphabet and phraseology are used in practice.

subcategories.name: Entertainment Learning
subcategories.description: Informal videos that include real radio calls.
subcategories.descriptionLong: Use these for extra exposure to the way operators speak on air.

categories.name: Podcasts & Audio
categories.descriptionLong: Audio is useful for hearing code words and procedural phrases at speed. Start with short clips, then move to longer recordings.

subcategories.name: Introductory Audio
subcategories.description: Short clips and slow practice material.
subcategories.descriptionLong: Begin with clear audio on single letters or short exchanges, then repeat what you hear.

subcategories.name: Intermediate Audio
subcategories.description: Longer recordings with connected speech.
subcategories.descriptionLong: These recordings put phrases into context and give you more to listen to in one sitting.

subcategories.name: Unscripted Audio
subcategories.description: Material made for an audience of operators.
subcategories.descriptionLong: This audio is not written for learners, so it reflects the pace and style of real radio work.

categories.name: Practice Games
categories.description: Short drills and quizzes for recall practice.
categories.descriptionLong: Games add a time limit or a score to your drills. They work best after you have seen the alphabet or phrase list once.

subcategories.name: Drill Games
subcategories.description: Scored practice with repeated prompts.
subcategories.descriptionLong: Use these drills to bring back a letter, code word, or abbreviation under time pressure.

subcategories.name: Scenario Practice
subcategories.description: Work through sample exchanges.
subcategories.descriptionLong: Read or watch a full exchange, then try to recall the wording used by each speaker.

subcategories.name: Educational Games
subcategories.description: Tools built for learning code.
subcategories.descriptionLong: These resources were designed to teach Morse or the spelling alphabet directly.

subcategories.name: Casual Practice
subcategories.description: Low pressure, short sessions.
subcategories.descriptionLong: Use a few minutes of casual practice to keep recent words fresh.

categories.name: ICAO Study Path
categories.description: Five stages for working through alphabet and phraseology practice.
categories.descriptionLong: These stages are a study order for this site. They are not official ICAO levels. Each stage groups material you can review before moving to the next.

subcategories.name: Stage 1: Alphabet
subcategories.description: Learn the twenty six code words.
subcategories.descriptionLong: Start with the letter to code word pairs and say each word out loud.

subcategories.name: Stage 2: Numbers
subcategories.description: Practice digits and common abbreviations.
subcategories.descriptionLong: Move on to numbers and short Q codes once the alphabet feels familiar.

subcategories.name: Stage 3: Standard Phrases
subcategories.description: Study routine radio exchanges.
subcategories.descriptionLong: Work on readbacks, call signs, and the stock phrases used in routine traffic.

subcategories.name: Stage 4: Callsigns
subcategories.description: Spell and exchange call signs.
subcategories.descriptionLong: Combine letters and numbers into full call signs, then check them against real examples.

subcategories.name: Stage 5: Emergencies
subcategories.description: Learn distress and urgency wording.
subcategories.descriptionLong: Finish with Mayday and related procedures, where exact wording matters most.

categories.name: Reading
categories.description: Documents and articles for reading radio material.
categories.descriptionLong: Reading official documents is slow going, but it gives you the exact wording used in procedures. Keep a short list of phrases as you read.

subcategories.name: Guided Reading
subcategories.description: Material that introduces terms in small steps.
subcategories.descriptionLong: Start with short explanations, then move to the official text once the vocabulary is familiar.

subcategories.name: Aviation News
subcategories.description: Reports and updates from aviation organisations.
subcategories.descriptionLong: News pages give you current material written for people who work in the field.

subcategories.name: Charts & Diagrams
subcategories.description: Visual material that supports a written explanation.
subcategories.descriptionLong: Use diagrams and illustrated guides to connect a phrase with the situation it describes.

subcategories.name: Long-Form Reading
subcategories.description: Manuals and books for extended study.
subcategories.descriptionLong: Long documents build stamina and show how terms are used across a whole procedure.

categories.name: Listening
categories.description: Audio drills for recognising words and phrases.
categories.descriptionLong: Listen first for the shape of a phrase, then for individual words. Repeating short clips is more useful than playing long recordings once.

subcategories.name: Audio Lessons
subcategories.description: Guided audio with explanations.
subcategories.descriptionLong: These lessons pair audio with teaching, so you can hear a phrase and learn what it means.

subcategories.name: Repeat Practice
subcategories.description: Material for listening and repeating.
subcategories.descriptionLong: Play a short clip, repeat it, and compare your timing with the original.

subcategories.name: Comprehension Practice
subcategories.description: Check that you understood what you heard.
subcategories.descriptionLong: Use these resources to test recall after a clip rather than simply playing it again.

categories.name: Speaking
categories.descriptionLong: The goal is to be understood on the first attempt. Slow down, keep the standard wording, and ask for a repeat when needed.

subcategories.name: Pronunciation
subcategories.description: Sources for the sounds and stress of code words.
subcategories.descriptionLong: Check how a word is said before you drill it, especially words that are easy to confuse.

subcategories.name: On-Air Practice
subcategories.description: Places to try full exchanges.
subcategories.descriptionLong: Once individual words are solid, practice complete calls with another person.

subcategories.name: Coaching & Tutoring
subcategories.description: Structured help from an experienced operator.
subcategories.descriptionLong: A tutor or local club can listen to your calls and correct your wording.

categories.name: Writing
categories.description: Written practice for call signs, abbreviations, and phrases.
categories.descriptionLong: Writing slows you down and makes errors visible. Use it to check spelling and to draft calls before you say them.

subcategories.name: Handwriting Practice
subcategories.description: Write letters, code words, and abbreviations by hand.
subcategories.descriptionLong: Writing each item once or twice helps when two code words look similar on paper.

subcategories.name: Message Drafting
subcategories.description: Put phrases together in the right order.
subcategories.descriptionLong: Draft a full call on paper, then read it back to check the sequence.

subcategories.name: Feedback & Correction
subcategories.description: Ask others to check your written work.
subcategories.descriptionLong: Post a short draft and ask for corrections to wording and order.

categories.name: Phraseology
categories.description: The rules and stock phrases used in radio calls.
categories.descriptionLong: Phraseology fixes the order and wording of a call so that both stations know what to expect. Learn the pattern before you vary it.

subcategories.name: Phraseology Guides
subcategories.description: Explanations of standard wording.
subcategories.descriptionLong: These guides describe which phrases are used in which situations.

subcategories.name: Phrase Practice
subcategories.description: Exercises that check your wording.
subcategories.descriptionLong: Use drills to practise the order of a call until it comes out naturally.

subcategories.name: Standard Phrases
subcategories.description: Fixed expressions for routine traffic.
subcategories.descriptionLong: Keep a short list of stock phrases and their meanings for quick review.

categories.name: Vocabulary
categories.description: Word lists for code words, abbreviations, and procedural terms.
categories.descriptionLong: Group words by topic and review them often. A short list you can recall is more useful than a long list you have only seen once.

subcategories.name: Core Lists
subcategories.description: The words worth learning first.
subcategories.descriptionLong: Start with the alphabet and the most common abbreviations.

subcategories.name: Themed Vocabulary
subcategories.description: Words grouped by subject.
subcategories.descriptionLong: Study distress wording or callsign terms together so you can see how they relate.

subcategories.name: Word Lists & Decks
subcategories.description: Ready made collections for review.
subcategories.descriptionLong: Pick a list, check that the entries are correct, and add it to your review routine.

categories.name: Code Words
categories.description: Reference and practice material for NATO code words.
categories.descriptionLong: Each letter has one assigned word. These resources help you learn the list, check it, and tell similar sounding words apart.

subcategories.name: Learning Systems
subcategories.description: Ways to learn the full list.
subcategories.descriptionLong: Use a fixed order or a review schedule to work through all twenty six words.

subcategories.name: Code Word Practice
subcategories.description: Drills for recall and spelling.
subcategories.descriptionLong: Practise both directions: letter to word and word to letter.

subcategories.name: Code Word Reference
subcategories.description: Tables and lists to check against.
subcategories.descriptionLong: Keep an authoritative list nearby when you are unsure of a word.

categories.name: Immersion
categories.description: Audio and video that give you extra exposure.
categories.descriptionLong: Use recorded material to hear how the alphabet and phraseology sound outside a lesson. Short, repeated clips are easiest to learn from.

subcategories.name: Media Tools
subcategories.description: Sites and pages that organise radio media.
subcategories.descriptionLong: These pages collect recorded material so you can find a short clip to study.

subcategories.name: Audio & Video
subcategories.description: Places with longer recordings and video.
subcategories.descriptionLong: Use these for background listening and for watching a full exchange.

subcategories.name: Phrase Mining
subcategories.description: Collect examples for your own review.
subcategories.descriptionLong: Save a phrase with its audio, then add it to a personal list for later practice.

categories.name: Community
categories.description: Forums and groups where radio questions get answered.
categories.descriptionLong: Other operators can explain what a phrase means in practice and correct your wording. Read the rules of each community before posting.

subcategories.name: Forums & Discussion
subcategories.description: Question and answer sites and subreddits.
subcategories.descriptionLong: Search first, then post a specific question if the answer is not already available.

subcategories.name: Live Chat
subcategories.description: Real time chat and group servers.
subcategories.descriptionLong: Live chat is useful for quick questions and for finding people to practise with.

subcategories.name: Practice Partners
subcategories.description: Clubs and partners for regular practice.
subcategories.descriptionLong: A regular partner or local club gives you a reason to use the phrases on a schedule.
